escalations.title: Vitest Arbitrary File Read/Execute (GHSA-5xrq-8626-4rwp)
escalations.exploit_scenario: When vitest UI server is listening on a non-localhost interface, an attacker sends an HTTP GET to the vitest UI port and reads/executes arbitrary project files. No authentication required.
escalations.impact: Remote Code Execution if vitest UI server is exposed to any network interface other than 127.0.0.1
escalations.recommendation: 1) Immediately verify vitest UI is NOT exposed (bind to localhost only or disable --ui flag). 2) Upgrade vitest to 4.1.10+.

escalations.title: Protobufjs Arbitrary Code Execution via gRPC (GHSA-xq3m-2v4x-88gg)
escalations.exploit_scenario: Orchestrator parses untrusted proto definitions from Docker API or gRPC endpoints. An attacker supplies a malicious proto message (bytes field default, option path, or recursive expansion) triggering unsafe code generation in protobufjs, achieving RCE on the orchestrator host.
escalations.impact: Complete orchestrator compromise. CVSS 9.8 — network-accessible, no authentication required.
escalations.recommendation: 1) Assess if orchestrator receives untrusted proto sources. 2) Upgrade dockerode 4.0.4 → 5.0.1+ to pull in patched protobufjs. 3) Or pin protobufjs >= 7.5.5 explicitly in lock file.
escalations.fix_blocker: Breaking change: dockerode 4→5 API migration required

escalations.title: Vite Path Traversal in Optimized Deps .map Handling (GHSA-4w7w-66w2-5vf9)
escalations.exploit_scenario: Attacker sends a crafted request to the Vite dev server for a .map file with a path-traversal sequence. The server resolves the path outside the allowed optimized-deps directory, exposing source maps or arbitrary project files.
escalations.impact: Source code / config disclosure from the Vite dev server. Production impact if source maps are bundled into production builds.
escalations.recommendation: Run npm audit fix in Source/Frontend and portal/Frontend. Verify vite is upgraded to ≥5.3.5 (check exact patched version).

findings.title: Traceability Enforcer CI Gate Reports False PASSED
findings.exploit_scenario: Developer runs `python3 tools/traceability-enforcer.py` and sees TRACEABILITY PASSED. They merge code with no coverage of 34+ plan FRs and 74 spec FRs. The CI gate never catches this because the enforcer only checks the most-recently-modified requirements.md.
findings.impact: Over 34 plan FRs and 74 spec FRs have zero implementation coverage — completely invisible to the CI gate. Any team trusting this gate believes coverage is complete when it is ~13%.
findings.recommendation: Change enforcer default to scan ALL Plans/*/requirements.md files and aggregate failures. CI gate command: `for f in Plans/*/requirements.md; do python3 tools/traceability-enforcer.py --file "$f" || exit 1; done`

findings.title: Specifications FR-001–FR-069 Completely Unimplemented (0% spec coverage)
findings.exploit_scenario: 74 domain FRs are defined in Specifications/ but have zero implementation in Source/. Stakeholders reviewing spec documents believe functionality exists; it does not.
findings.impact: Spec-implementation gap is invisible due to QO-001. If the Specifications represent committed deliverables, the entire feature set is missing.
findings.recommendation: Clarify intent: (a) phase-gated delivery — add Phase-N headers to spec sections; update CLAUDE.md. (b) superseded — archive with notes. Either way, update enforcer to detect the gap.

findings.title: Routes Import Store Directly — Service Layer Bypassed
findings.exploit_scenario: A new coder adds a CRUD route and calls store.createWorkItem() directly, skipping change-history tracking in changeHistory.ts, resulting in silent data corruption.
findings.impact: Business validation logic lives in route handlers rather than services; untestable in isolation. Architectural rule violation per CLAUDE.md.
findings.recommendation: Extract WorkItemService that owns all store calls. Route handlers call service methods; services call the store. Remove all store/ imports from route files.

findings.title: OpenTelemetry Tracing Not Implemented — Mandatory Architecture Rule Violated
findings.exploit_scenario: A production incident occurs. Engineers have no distributed traces to diagnose which workflow stage failed or how long each step took. Prometheus metrics alone cannot reconstruct request flow.
findings.impact: Zero distributed tracing across the application. Non-negotiable architecture requirement completely absent.
findings.recommendation: Add @opentelemetry/sdk-node, @opentelemetry/auto-instrumentations-node. Configure in src/telemetry.ts loaded before app.ts. Add custom spans in router.ts and assessment.ts. Add traceparent header propagation.
findings.cross_ref: [CROSS-REF: dependency-auditor] portal/Backend already has OTel packages — reference that implementation

findings.title: Duplicate Test Files — Vitest Runs Both Copies
findings.exploit_scenario: A developer fixes a bug verified by the tests/pages/ version but accidentally breaks the root-level version's mock contract. CI passes because pages/ tests pass, but the root-level tests flag a different regression attributed to the same test file name.
findings.impact: 39 redundant test cases inflate pass count. Divergent mock setups may test subtly different behaviors, masking regressions.
findings.recommendation: Delete root-level duplicates (tests/WorkItemDetailPage.test.tsx, tests/WorkItemListPage.test.tsx). Add explicit test.include: ['tests/**/*.test.*'] to vite.config.ts.

findings.title: form-data CRLF Injection in Multipart Field Names (GHSA-hmw2-7cc7-3qxx)
findings.exploit_scenario: Attacker crafts a multipart field name containing CRLF characters. The form-data library emits the unescaped characters into the HTTP headers, injecting arbitrary headers or content (cache poisoning, request smuggling).
findings.recommendation: Run npm audit fix in Source/Frontend and platform/orchestrator to pull in form-data@4.0.6+.

findings.title: ws WebSocket Uninitialized Memory Disclosure & DoS (GHSA-58qx-3vcg-4xpx)
findings.exploit_scenario: Attacker sends malformed WebSocket frames causing server to leak uninitialized buffer memory. Alternatively, sends tiny fragments to exhaust server memory via unbounded buffering.
findings.recommendation: Upgrade vitest/vite to pull in patched ws version. Track fix availability upstream.

findings.title: React Router Protocol-Relative URL Open Redirect (GHSA-2j2x-hqr9-3h42)
findings.exploit_scenario: Attacker crafts a link to //attacker.com via a user-controlled redirect parameter. React Router <6.30.4 treats the double-slash path as protocol-relative, causing the browser to navigate to the attacker's domain.
findings.recommendation: npm install react-router-dom@6.30.4 in Source/Frontend — straightforward patch-level upgrade within v6.

findings.title: @grpc/grpc-js Server Crash on Malformed Requests (GHSA-5375-pq7m-f5r2)
findings.exploit_scenario: Attacker sends a malformed or compressed gRPC message to the orchestrator. The gRPC server crashes with an unhandled exception, taking down the orchestrator process.

findings.title: path-to-regexp Regular Expression Denial of Service (GHSA-37ch-88jc-xwx2)
findings.exploit_scenario: Attacker crafts a URL with repeating route parameters (e.g. /a/:x/:y/:z/:z/:z/:z) causing catastrophic regex backtracking in path-to-regexp. The event loop blocks for seconds, DoS-ing the orchestrator API.
findings.recommendation: Upgrade express to v5 in platform/orchestrator (breaking change — requires API review). Or pin path-to-regexp to a fixed version.

findings.title: @opentelemetry High-Severity CVEs in Portal Backend
findings.exploit_scenario: Uncharacterized high-severity CVEs in OpenTelemetry packages used by portal/Backend. Exact attack vector requires manual npm audit.
findings.recommendation: cd portal/Backend && npm audit fix. Review audit output manually.

findings.title: dependency-linking Requirements Reference Stale portal/ Paths
findings.recommendation: Update requirements.md to use Source/ paths and current FR-dependency-* IDs so the enforcer can validate these features.

findings.title: Dual Logger Abstraction — Two Logger Files with Different Interfaces
findings.recommendation: Pick utils/logger.ts as canonical. Update all callers of the shim. Delete src/logger.ts.

findings.title: eslint-disable suppressions Without Documented Justification
findings.recommendation: Investigate both react-hooks/exhaustive-deps disables. If intentional: add justification comment. If stale-closure bug: fix the hook.

findings.title: DebugPortalPage Uses Non-conformant Traceability ID Format
findings.recommendation: Create a spec FR for the debug portal page and assign an FR-WF-XXX ID, or document it as an exception in CLAUDE.md.

p4_findings.title: License Compliance — PASS
p4_findings.detail: No GPL/AGPL/restrictive licenses detected. All direct dependencies use MIT or Apache-2.0.

p4_findings.title: Supply Chain Risk — LOW
p4_findings.detail: All packages have institutional backing. No single-maintainer risk for critical deps. High download counts. No deprecated packages.
